Binge drinking every 2 weeks, smoker. RLQ rigidity + guarding + rebound, right adnexal tenderness, uterus slightly enlarged with dark bloody discharge. HR 110, BP 70 — hemorrhagic shock from ruptured ectopic.

history.hpi: 33F, sudden onset lower abdominal pain x3 hours, vomiting, malaise. No trauma. Last menstrual period 19 days ago. Mid-cycle spotting. Prior infertility — required multiple rounds of fertility medications to conceive her only child, now age 5.
history.obgyn: G2P1. Fertility medications for prior pregnancy. Divorced. Unprotected sex while intoxicated at a party. No birth control — believes she cannot conceive. LMP 19 days ago. Mid-cycle spotting. Last PAP was normal one year ago.
history.social: Divorced. Lives with 5-year-old daughter. Binge drinks every 2 weeks since divorce. Smokes cigarettes (won't smoke in home or near daughter). No marijuana or illicit drugs. Insurance professional, college degree.

physicalExam.general: Moderate distress, pale, anxious, clutching lower abdomen
physicalExam.abdomen: RLQ tenderness to palpation and percussion. Rigidity, guarding, AND rebound tenderness present. No masses or organomegaly. Bowel sounds normoactive.
physicalExam.pelvic: Right adnexal tenderness. Uterus slightly enlarged. Small amount of dark bloody discharge from cervix.
physicalExam.rectal: Sphincter tone normal. Stool brown, no occult blood.

missedOrders.why: Pre-operative clearance. She needs emergency surgery. Every surgical patient needs a pre-op EKG to rule out arrhythmia before anesthesia.
Transvaginal ultrasound is the gold standard for ectopic pregnancy diagnosis. Empty uterus + adnexal mass + free fluid = ruptured ectopic. Transabdominal may miss it. TVUS is definitive.
Patient is vomiting. Control nausea before OR. Ondansetron is pregnancy-safe.

missedOrders.order: Type and screen / Type and Rh factor
missedOrders.why: Pre-op labs. Blood must be available before she bleeds out on the table. Also need Rh type — if Rh-negative, RhoGAM is indicated for any bleeding in pregnancy.
Severe pain in a crashing patient. NSAIDs contraindicated — she's about to go to OR. Opioids are safe in pregnancy for acute surgical pain.

missedOrders.order: Laparotomy / Laparoscopy / OB-GYN consult / Surgery consult
missedOrders.why: This is the treatment. Ruptured ectopic = immediate surgery. The patient is actively hemorrhaging. Every minute in the ED without a surgeon is a minute of continued intraperitoneal bleeding. Case timed out because surgery was never ordered.
Unprotected sex led to this ectopic. She thinks she's infertile — education needed.
Smoking is a risk factor for ectopic pregnancy. Also general health.
Binge drinking every 2 weeks since divorce. Heavy alcohol use impairs judgment — including the decision to have unprotected sex while intoxicated.
Unprotected sex. STIs (particularly chlamydia) are a major risk factor for ectopic pregnancy via tubal damage from PID. Screen now, treat if positive.

pathophysiology.ectopicImplantation: Fertilized ovum implants outside the uterine cavity — 95% in the fallopian tube (ampulla > isthmus > fimbria). The tube cannot expand like the uterus. As the embryo grows, it invades the tubal wall, erodes into blood vessels, and eventually ruptures the tube.
pathophysiology.riskFactors: Smoking, infertility (altered tubal motility from fertility medications?), unprotected sex with potential for undiagnosed chlamydia → tubal damage from subclinical PID. Divorced, binge drinking → impaired judgment → unprotected sex.
pathophysiology.peritonealIrritation: Blood is an irritant to the peritoneum. Rigidity, guarding, rebound = chemical peritonitis from intraperitoneal blood.
pathophysiology.hemorrhagicShock: HR 110, BP 70. Tachycardia is the FIRST sign of hemorrhagic shock — the heart compensates for falling stroke volume by increasing rate. Hypotension is a LATE sign. She's Class II-III hemorrhagic shock.
pathophysiology.darkBloodyDischarge: Decidual cast — the uterine lining sheds because the ectopic doesn't produce enough hCG to maintain it. This is a soft sign of ectopic: vaginal bleeding + empty uterus on US + positive β-hCG + adnexal mass.

teachingPoints: Ectopic pregnancy is the #1 cause of maternal mortality in the first trimester. Every reproductive-age woman with pelvic pain is ectopic until the β-hCG and US say otherwise.
Hemorrhagic shock = tachycardia FIRST, hypotension LATER. If you wait for the BP to drop, she's already Class II-III.
Diagnosis is not the same as treatment. You can nail the diagnosis and still lose the patient if you don't advance to surgery.
TVUS is the gold standard. CT and X-ray are contraindicated in a positive pregnancy test.
Type and screen BEFORE she crashes. OR consult ASAP. Every minute of delay is continued intraperitoneal hemorrhage.
Methotrexate is for STABLE ectopics. She's hypotensive and tachycardic with peritoneal signs — she goes to OR, not to MTX.
Preventive care matters: safe sex counseling, smoking cessation, alcohol counseling, STI screening. 0% on all of it.
